page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text: catchword at the right and gathering signature at the left. The header carries the running head and a page number.

p.i: liati servabimur per vitam ipsius, hoc est, si e-nim cum ipsius inimici essemus adeo nos dilexit, ut Filium suum pro nobis in mortem daret, et nos ISTA RATIONE SIBI reconciliare voluerit; multo magis postquam ipsi reconciliati sumus per eundem filium suum in coelesti gloria viventem ab aeterna morte nos servabit.

main_text.p: Hic certè actualis illa reconciliatio nostri facta per nostri justificationem & conversionem, non excludit, sed includit seu præsupponit reconciliationem Dei nobiscum factam per mortem & sanguinē crucis Christi. Deinde Mortis & Vitæ Christi mentionem eo trahi non debere concedo, quasi illa minus, hæc magis efficax sit ad nos servandū, sed hoc tantum dici, justificatos per Christum viventem eo magis iri servatum, quia jam non necesse sit Christū amplius IPSORUM CAUSA MORI.

2. Deum nos sibi per Christum recō-2. Deum nos sibi per Christum reconciliasse. ciliasse legimus. 2. Corin. 5. Omnia haec, inquit Apostolus, Paraphrasis est loci. pendent ab auctore Deo, qui per Iesum Christum omnia instauravit, nosque fideles per illius ministerium sibi reconciliavit: denique[?] nobis Apostolis huius reconciliationis administrationem commisit. Equidem ipse

page.notes: The printed page carries a handwritten or stamped "258" in the upper right corner; it is not printed text and is left out. The first word "liati" is a fragment at the page top and is kept as printed. The catchword "Deum" is partly cut and read with doubt. The page number "55" is read with doubt. "denique" is written as the scan suggests (q with tilde), with [?]. The marginal notes are small and partly cut at the right edge; the note wording is reconstructed from the visible letters. Long s is normalised to s throughout.
